body_en: Democrats ask judge to dismiss Trump administration’s challenge to Alaska Senate race
IE 11 is not supported. For an optimal experience visit our site on another browser.

Attorneys for Alaska’s Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola and Senate Democrats filed a motion Friday urging a federal judge to drop the Trump administration’s lawsuit that seeks to block the results of the upcoming election if Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan loses.

The motion, filed on behalf of Peltola’s campaign and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, called the lawsuit filed by the Justice Department “an unprecedented pre-emptive strike on democratic elections.”

“This case directly threatens both Proposed Intervenors’ interests by demanding that defendants refuse to certify the election if, and only if, Peltola wins,” the filing said. “It is part of a nationwide attack on free elections by the federal government, which the DSCC has fought at every turn.”

The Trump administration filed suit against election officials in Alaska Thursday, arguing that candidate Dan J. Sullivan Jr.’s appearance on the ballot could mislead those who wish to vote for Sen. Dan S. Sullivan’s re-election.
The lawsuit came after President Donald Trump repeatedly complained about both the incumbent being threatened by a man with the same name and the state’s use of ranked-choice voting.

“I am very concerned about the Dan S. Sullivan Race for the U.S. Senate in Alaska in that it is totally confusing,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post Wednesday. “It’s ridiculous that the Court didn’t stop this SCAM.”

The DOJ’s lawsuit asks the court to block the Alaska Senate results from being certified if Dan S. Sullivan does not win the election, and if “had all votes cast for Dan J. Sullivan been cast instead for Senator Sullivan and Alaska’s rank-choice process played out accordingly, Senator Sullivan would have won the election.”

The filing from Peltola and Senate Democrats pushes back against this request, stating that “the Department of Justice’s assumption that every voter who casts a vote for Dan J. Sullivan really meant to vote for Senator Sullivan is insulting to voters and irreconcilable with Alaska’s ranked choice voting procedures and the ballot’s clear differentiation between the two candidates.”

“Alaskans for Mary and DSCC are entitled to intervene as of right to defend against the Department of Justice’s extraordinary assault,” the motion said. “And there is reason to doubt that the existing defendants will vigorously defend against DOJ’s demands, given their effort to exclude Daniel J. Sullivan from the ballot earlier this year.”

After Dan J. Sullivan Jr. was removed from the ballot in June after election officials decided his candidacy was “not in good faith,” a judge in Alaska overturned the decision later that month, validating his campaign.
Trump has claimed that Dan J. Sullivan Jr. is only running because “Democrats put him up as a matter of confusion,” calling his candidacy “corrupt.” Dan J. Sullivan Jr. has denied the allegations.

NBC News reported in July that federal and state investigators were looking into whether Dan J. Sullivan Jr. could be part of a conspiracy to confuse voters, according to two people who had knowledge of the situation.
The DOJ’s lawsuit comes less than two weeks ahead of Election Day and after the state has begun early voting. The court has not yet set a hearing date for the suit.
Legal and election experts told NBC News that the DOJ’s case is on shaky ground.
As U.S. elections are run and certified by state and local officials, rather than the federal government, the law limits the Justice Department’s role in elections.

The nonpartisan Cook Political Report rated the Alaska Senate contest as a “toss-up.” The race marks a critical opportunity for Democrats to take a seat from Republicans as they vie for control of the Senate.
Kyla Guilfoil is a breaking news reporter on the politics team for NBC News Digital.
body_zh: 民主党人要求法官驳回特朗普政府对阿拉斯加州参议员竞选的挑战

阿拉斯加民主党参议院候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉和参议院民主党人的律师周五提交了一项动议，敦促联邦法官撤销特朗普政府的诉讼，该诉讼旨在阻止即将到来的选举结果，如果共和党现任总统丹·S·沙利文输了。
该动议代表佩尔托拉的竞选团队和民主党参议员竞选委员会提出，称司法部提起的诉讼是“对民主选举前所未有的先发制人的打击”。
文件称：“本案要求被告在且仅当佩尔托拉获胜时拒绝认证选举，从而直接威胁到拟议干预者的利益。” “这是联邦政府对自由选举进行的全国性攻击的一部分，DSCC 一直在与这种攻击作斗争。”
特朗普政府周四对阿拉斯加州的选举官员提起诉讼，称候选人小丹·沙利文出现在选票上可能会误导那些希望投票支持参议员丹·沙利文连任的人。
这起诉讼是在唐纳德·特朗普总统多次抱怨现任总统受到同名男子的威胁以及该州使用排名选择投票之后发生的。
“我对丹·S·沙利文在阿拉斯加竞选美国参议员感到非常担忧，因为这完全令人困惑，”特朗普周三在《真相社会》帖子中写道。 “法庭没有阻止这种骗局，真是可笑。”
司法部的诉讼要求法院，如果丹·S·沙利文没有赢得选举，则法院阻止阿拉斯加州参议院的结果得到认证，并且如果“如果所有投票给丹·J·沙利文，而不是参议员沙利文，并且阿拉斯加州的排名选择过程相应地进行，沙利文参议员就会赢得选举。”
佩尔托拉和参议院民主党人提交的文件反驳了这一请求，指出“司法部认为每一位投票给丹·J·沙利文的选民实际上都是为了投票给沙利文参议员，这是对选民的侮辱，并且与阿拉斯加州的排名选择投票程序以及投票中两位候选人之间的明显区别是不可调和的。”
动议称：“阿拉斯加玛丽和 DSCC 有权进行干预，以抵御司法部的非同寻常的攻击。” “鉴于今年早些时候他们努力将丹尼尔·J·沙利文排除在投票之外，我们有理由怀疑现有被告是否会积极抗辩司法部的要求。”
6 月，选举官员认定小丹·J·沙利文的候选资格“并非出于善意”，因此将其从选票中除名。阿拉斯加州的一名法官于当月晚些时候推翻了这一决定，证实了他的竞选活动。
特朗普声称，小丹·J·沙利文参加竞选只是因为“民主党人把他当作一个混乱的问题”，称他的候选资格“腐败”。小丹·J·沙利文 (Dan J. Sullivan Jr.) 否认了这些指控。
据两名知情人士透露，美国全国广播公司新闻 (NBC News) 7 月份报道称，联邦和州调查人员正在调查小丹·J·沙利文 (Dan J. Sullivan Jr.) 是否参与了迷惑选民的阴谋。
司法部的诉讼是在距离选举日不到两周且该州开始提前投票之后提出的。法院尚未确定该诉讼的听证日期。
法律和选举专家告诉 NBC 新闻，司法部的案件基础不牢。
由于美国选举是由州和地方官员而不是联邦政府进行和认证的，因此法律限制了司法部在选举中的作用。
无党派的库克政治报告将阿拉斯加参议院的竞选评为“难以预测”。这次竞选标志着民主党在争夺参议院控制权时从共和党手中夺取席位的关键机会。
Kyla Guilfoil 是 NBC News Digital 政治团队的突发新闻记者。

title_en: Ex-FBI employees charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden inquiries
title_zh: 前联邦调查局雇员被控在亨特·拜登调查中向国会撒谎
summary: Republicans have long accused the FBI of mishandling the laptop and the investigations into the younger Biden.

body_en: Two former FBI agents charged over Hunter Biden probes : NPR
Two former FBI agents charged over Hunter Biden probes Republicans have long accused the FBI of mishandling the laptop and the investigations into the younger Biden.
Ex-FBI employees charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden inquiries

The Justice Department has charged two former FBI employees with making false statements to Congress in connection with the bureau's investigations into Hunter Biden and his laptop ahead of the 2020 presidential election.

Bradley Benavides and Nikki Floris each face a single criminal count stemming from testimony before lawmakers in 2023. The pair, who held senior positions on the FBI's now defunct Foreign Influence Task Force, both turned themselves in and made their initial court appearance Friday morning in Washington, D.C.

The new prosecution is the latest politically fraught case to be brought by the Justice Department since President Trump returned to the White House. It dredges back up the bizarre saga surrounding former President Joe Biden's son, Hunter Biden, and his various legal troubles that featured throughout the 2020 presidential campaign.

Hunter Biden's laptop was the subject of intense scrutiny after The New York Post reported weeks before the 2020 presidential election that the device was abandoned at a Delaware repair shop in 2019, and then obtained by President Trump's former personal lawyer Rudy Giuliani.

Republicans have long accused the FBI of mishandling the laptop and the investigations into the younger Biden. Hunter Biden was convicted of federal gun charges and later pleaded guilty to separate tax offenses. (Joe Biden signed a full and unconditional pardon for his son in December 2024.)

In a statement on X , the U.S. attorney for Washington, D.C., Jeanine Pirro, said Floris and Benavides "allegedly lied to Congress about their roles in the FBI's Hunter Biden investigations, with one claiming they only learned about it from Wikipedia — despite evidence showing their involvement in helping shape the public narrative about Hunter Biden's laptop right before the election."

Prosecutors charged Benavides and Floris by criminal complaint, which means prosecutors have yet to secure an indictment from a grand jury. Under the second Trump administration, grand juries in the nation's capital and other cities have refused on several occasions to return indictments in high-profile, politically charged cases.

At a court hearing Friday morning, Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui noted that both of the defendants have "sparkling backgrounds" in federal law enforcement and were longtime dedicated public servants. He also noted that charging them by criminal complaint for conduct that is "quite old" is unusual.
Benavides, 56, and Floris, 46, are due back in court for a preliminary hearing on Tuesday.
In a statement, Floris' attorneys called her a "patriot" who served as "dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years."

"Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts. It's no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election," they added.
Agents search Rep. Omar's D.C. home; DOJ says it's part of criminal investigation

The Post reported Hunter Biden's laptop showed wrongdoing by then-Democratic nominee Joe Biden, who subsequently won the election. Some of the data on the laptop was later ascertained to belong to Hunter Biden. House Republicans subsequently launched an impeachment inquiry into President Biden, focusing on Hunter Biden's business dealings at the time his father was vice president. But no evidence has ever been presented that Joe Biden financially gained from his son's business activities.
The complaint alleges that Benavides and Floris both had real-time knowledge of the Hunter Biden investigations, including into his laptop, in their top posts on the Foreign Influence Task Force.
But in interviews with the House Judiciary Committee in 2023, both of them allegedly lied about their knowledge and involvement in those investigations.

Those purported false statements were material to the committee's investigation, the complaint says, because they allowed both Benavides and Floris to "escape" further questioning about Hunter Biden, which hindered the panel's investigation.

前联邦调查局雇员被控在亨特·拜登调查中向国会撒谎
更新于 2026 年 10 月 23 日下午 2:50（美国东部时间） 最初发布于 2026 年 10 月 23 日上午 11:51（美国东部时间）
前总统乔·拜登的儿子亨特·拜登于 2024 年 7 月出现在华盛顿特区。安娜摇钱树/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
司法部指控两名前联邦调查局雇员在 2020 年总统大选前调查亨特·拜登及其笔记本电脑时向国会做出虚假陈述。
布拉德利·贝纳维德斯 (Bradley Benavides) 和尼基·弗洛里斯 (Nikki Floris) 均因 2023 年在立法者面前作证而面临一项刑事指控。两人曾在联邦调查局 (FBI) 现已解散的外国影响特别工作组中担任高级职务，两人均于周五上午在华盛顿特区自首并首次出庭。
新的起诉是特朗普总统重返白宫以来司法部提起的最新一起充满政治争议的案件。它挖掘了围绕前总统乔·拜登之子亨特·拜登的离奇传奇，以及他在 2020 年总统竞选期间遇到的各种法律麻烦。
在 2020 年总统大选前几周，《纽约邮报》报道称，亨特·拜登的笔记本电脑于 2019 年被遗弃在特拉华州的一家维修店，随后被特朗普总统的前私人律师鲁迪·朱利安尼获得，此后，亨特·拜登的笔记本电脑成为了严格审查的对象。
共和党人长期以来一直指责联邦调查局对笔记本电脑和对年轻拜登的调查处理不当。亨特·拜登被判犯有联邦枪支罪，后来承认了单独的税务犯罪。 （乔·拜登于 2024 年 12 月签署了对其儿子的全面无条件赦免。）
华盛顿特区联邦检察官珍妮·皮罗 (Jeanine Pirro) 在 X 网站上发表的一份声明中表示，弗洛里斯和贝纳维德斯“据称就他们在联邦调查局亨特·拜登调查中的角色向国会撒谎，其中一人声称他们只是从维基百科了解到此事，尽管有证据表明他们参与了在大选前帮助塑造有关亨特·拜登笔记本电脑的公众叙述。”
检察官对贝纳维德斯和弗洛里斯提起刑事诉讼，这意味着检察官尚未获得大陪审团的起诉。在特朗普第二届政府执政期间，美国首都和其他城市的大陪审团多次拒绝对备受瞩目的政治指控案件发出起诉书。
在周五上午的法庭听证会上，治安法官齐亚·法鲁基指出，两名被告在联邦执法部门都有“耀眼的背景”，并且是长期敬业的公务员。他还指出，通过刑事诉讼指控他们的行为“相当古老”，这是不寻常的。
56 岁的贝纳维德斯和 46 岁的弗洛里斯将于周二返回法庭参加初步听证会。
弗洛里斯的律师在一份声明中称她为“爱国者”，“担任联邦调查局情报官员近 20 年”。
“然而今天，司法部根据政客的说法，而不是根据事实，错误地指控她犯罪。几年后，在选举前夕，政府提出这些无稽之谈的指控并非巧合，”他们补充道。
特工搜查众议员奥马尔在华盛顿的家；美国司法部表示这是刑事调查的一部分
据《华盛顿邮报》报道，亨特·拜登的笔记本电脑显示当时的民主党候选人乔·拜登有不当行为，后者随后赢得了选举。后来确定笔记本电脑上的一些数据属于亨特·拜登。众议院共和党人随后对拜登总统发起弹劾调查，重点关注亨特·拜登在其父亲担任副总统期间的商业交易。但没有证据表明乔·拜登从儿子的商业活动中获得了经济利益。
起诉书称，贝纳维德斯和弗洛里斯都在外国影响力特别工作组的高层帖子中实时了解了亨特·拜登的调查情况，包括他的笔记本电脑。

Week in Politics: Ramaswamy’s Ohio ad; Trump greenlights DOJ to sue over Alaska Senate Ohio GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy refuses to withdrawal an explosive attack ad, and President Trump greenlights the DOJ to file a lawsuit about Alaska's senate race.
Week in Politics: Ramaswamy's Ohio ad; Trump greenlights DOJ to sue over Alaska Senate
Ohio GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy refuses to withdrawal an explosive attack ad, and President Trump greenlights the DOJ to file a lawsuit about Alaska's senate race.

Midterm politics grew especially ugly this week in Ohio. The Republican candidate for governor, Vivek Ramaswamy, released an attack ad against his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton. The ad featured Acton's estranged mother who called her daughter a liar and urged Ohioans not to vote for her. But a lot of context - much of it sad and upsetting - was missing from that ad. And before we go on, please be aware we're about to talk about allegations of sexual abuse. NPR senior political contributor Ron Elving joins us. Ron, thanks for being with us.
RON ELVING, BYLINE: Good to be with you, Scott.

SIMON: Legal documents from nearly 50 years ago show that Amy Acton, then 12, and her younger brother were removed from their mother's home following their stepfather's arrest. He was charged with sexual conduct with a minor, fled the state with their mother. He died without facing trial. Amy Acton says he raped her and that she had been sexually abused beginning when she was just 9 years old. The ad has been condemned, including by the current Republican governor, and yet, Ramaswamy continues to defend it. Why?

ELVING: There's an old expression I think we all know - in for a dime in for a dollar. If you're going to risk your statewide campaign and the tens of millions of dollars that Elon Musk and others have invested in it, if you are already risking all that on this kind of tactics - this ad that's divided the Republican Party in Ohio and nationally - then it's not surprising that you choose to defend it. The same goes for Ramaswamy backers, like Vice President JD Vance, who condemned, but rather Republicans who criticized it, calling them whiners - or, for that matter, President Trump, who could have easily stayed out of it but waded in with both feet, telling Ramaswamy to keep the ad running.
SIMON: Is this something with a potential damage to not just Ramaswamy, but other Republicans this election?

ELVING: It might well be in Ohio, where this has dominated conversation, it could blow back on the party's embattled Senate incumbent, Jon Husted, who's in a tight race for reelection against Democratic former Senator Sherrod Brown. Beyond that, any campaigning of this sort, any controversy like this, it just tends to be dispiriting and may discourage people who don't just automatically turn out for midterms.

SIMON: Yesterday, with less than two weeks to go in this election, the Department of Justice filed a lawsuit with a special request of a federal judge about the U.S. Senate race in Alaska. Please tell us about this.

ELVING: Yes. The state of Alaska has a ranked-choice system where the primary election sends several top finishers on to November regardless of party. So the incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan is on the ballot as a Republican, and there's another Dan Sullivan - different middle initial - who also got enough primary votes for the fall ballot. Now, he's not the official Republican Party candidate, even though he's a registered Republican. That's legal in Alaska, but it angered the president, so he sent in the Justice Department to sue to block the certification of results in this election if Trump's preferred Dan Sullivan doesn't win.

We saw Trump in his first term getting angry with people in his Justice Department who pushed back on some of his orders, who chose to follow the law and previous policy instead. Trump has since tried to get rid of those people and replace them with lawyers who will do what he wants. So there are many who fear what might be next if Trump isn't pleased with the election results around the country 10 days from now.
SIMON: Ron, I understand the Brewers were going to call you in to pinch hit last night but won despite that. What's it feel like in Milwaukee?
ELVING: (Laughter) Oh, my goodness. You and I both grew up in Chicago, Scott. We're Cub fans for life, but it turns out that grandsons have a way of scrambling even one's baseball loyalties.
SIMON: Well, NPR's Ron Elving. Thanks so much for being with us.

俄亥俄州共和党州长候选人维韦克·拉马斯瓦米拒绝撤回爆炸性攻击广告，特朗普总统批准司法部就阿拉斯加州参议员竞选提起诉讼。
本周俄亥俄州的中期选举政治变得尤其丑陋。共和党州长候选人维韦克·拉马斯瓦米发布了一则攻击民主党对手艾米·阿克顿的广告。该广告以阿克顿关系疏远的母亲为主角，她称她的女儿是骗子，并敦促俄亥俄州人不要投票给她。但该广告缺少很多背景信息——其中大部分是悲伤和令人不安的。在我们继续之前，请注意我们将讨论性虐待指控。 NPR 高级政治撰稿人 Ron Elving 加入我们。罗恩，谢谢你和我们在一起。
罗恩·埃尔文连线：很高兴和你在一起，斯科特。
西蒙：近 50 年前的法律文件显示，继父被捕后，当时 12 岁的艾米·阿克顿 (Amy Acton) 和她的弟弟被从母亲的家中带走。他被指控与未成年人发生性行为，并与母亲逃离该州。他未经审判就去世了。艾米·阿克顿 (Amy Acton) 称，他强奸了她，而她从 9 岁起就开始遭受性虐待。该广告遭到了包括现任共和党州长在内的谴责，但拉马斯瓦米仍在继续为其辩护。为什么？

ELVING：我想我们都知道一个古老的表达方式——一分钱一分货。如果你要拿全州竞选活动以及埃隆·马斯克和其他人投入的数千万美元冒险，如果你已经在这种策略上冒着所有风险——这则广告在俄亥俄州和全国范围内分裂了共和党——那么你选择捍卫它就不足为奇了。拉马斯瓦米的支持者也是如此，比如副总统万斯（JD Vance）谴责了这一做法，而共和党人则批评了拉马斯瓦米，称他们为牢骚者——或者就这一点而言，特朗普总统本可以轻易置身事外，但却双脚介入，告诉拉马斯瓦米继续投放广告。
西蒙：这是否不仅会对拉马斯瓦米造成潜在损害，还会对本次选举的其他共和党人造成潜在损害？
埃尔文：很可能在俄亥俄州，这件事在当地占据主导地位，这可能会对该党陷入困境的现任参议院议员乔恩·赫斯特德(Jon Husted)造成回击，他正在与民主党前参议员谢罗德·布朗(Sherrod Brown)争夺连任。除此之外，任何此类竞选活动、任何此类争议，都往往会令人沮丧，并可能使那些不自动参加中期选举的人灰心丧气。
西蒙：昨天，距离本次选举还有不到两周的时间，司法部就阿拉斯加的美国参议院竞选向联邦法官提起了一项特别请求。请告诉我们这件事。

埃尔文：是的。阿拉斯加州有一个排名选择制度，初选将几名排名前列的人选入 11 月，无论党派如何。因此，现任参议员丹·沙利文作为共和党人参加了选票，还有另一位丹·沙利文——中间名首字母不同——也为秋季投票获得了足够的初选票。现在，他不是正式的共和党候选人，尽管他是注册的共和党人。这在阿拉斯加是合法的，但这激怒了总统，因此如果特朗普喜欢的丹·沙利文没有获胜，他派司法部提起诉讼，阻止对这次选举结果的认证。
我们看到特朗普在他的第一个任期内对司法部的人感到愤怒，这些人拒绝了他的一些命令，而是选择遵守法律和之前的政策。此后，特朗普试图摆脱这些人，并用愿意做他想做的事情的律师取而代之。因此，很多人担心，如果特朗普对 10 天后全国各地的选举结果不满意，接下来会发生什么。
西蒙：罗恩，我知道酿酒人队昨晚打算叫你来代打，但尽管如此还是赢了。在 密尔沃基 是什么感觉？
埃尔文：（笑声）哦，天哪。你和我都在芝加哥长大，斯科特。我们一生都是小熊队的球迷，但事实证明，孙子们甚至有办法扰乱一个人对棒球的忠诚度。

body_en: California election officials frustrated, rattled by DOJ demand to sequester 'noncitizen' ballots
Local election officials in California are frustrated after receiving a letter from the U.S. Department of Justice

Los Angeles -- Local election officials across California are confused and frustrated after receiving letters from President Donald Trump's Justice Department demanding that county registrars sequester ballots that the federal government believes were sent to noncitizen voters ahead of the midterm elections.

The letters, which were sent on Friday , ask for sensitive information, including Social Security numbers, on roughly 20,000 voters. It is illegal for noncitizens to register to vote or cast a ballot. The administration has insisted that immigrants voting is a major problem nationwide, when in fact it is quite rare , as even its own investigations have shown.
“All of this is simply meant to raise huge doubts about the integrity of this election,” said John Tuteur, the registrar of voters for Napa County in California’s wine country.
The Justice Department did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment on Saturday.
Tuteur and other election officials who spoke to The Associated Press on Saturday said they have already started to count ballots that have trickled in from the state's 23 million registered voters.
“We’re not changing anything we’re doing. We’re proceeding with the election,” he said.
The federal government set a 48-hour deadline to provide information, and it warned that legal action could be taken against any official who knowingly counted a noncitizen's vote.

However, the California attorney general's office said the letters contained errors. For example, Mendocino County officials received a list of people who were not residents there, according to the state's court filing.

The letters are the latest escalation in a legal battle between Democratic-dominated California and Trump's Department of Justice ahead of the midterms. The federal government sued on Oct. 15, roughly three weeks before elections, asking a judge to bar the state from counting mail-in ballots from people the federal government has identified as likely noncitizens. A panel of 9th Circuit appeals court judges will hear arguments on Sunday about whether California can be compelled to comply with the federal government’s demands.

Tuteur said that two uniformed Department of Homeland Security officers delivered a letter to his office late on Friday afternoon. The letter included the names of 42 people who the federal government accused of being noncitizens illegally registered to vote. There are roughly 86,000 people registered to vote across the county of over 130,000 people, Tuteur said. Approximately 11,000 people had already cast a mail-in ballot as of Friday. In larger counties like Los Angeles, that number has already reached over 331,000 counted mail-in votes.
He said his employees and his relatives were worried about what could come next.

“My family’s upset, worried about what’s going to happen to me,” he said.

The letter sent to Clerk-Recorder Kim Grady's office in rural Amador County listed four people allegedly illegally registered to vote in the county. Grady was waiting on more guidance from the state about what she should do, and she wasn't sure if she would get any clarity before the deadline.

The letters on Friday came on the heels of a statewide sweep by federal authorities on Monday, where 28 people from the list of 20,000 were charged with illegally registering to vote. Some were also charged with illegally voting and lying on naturalization paperwork. Those charges could lead to years in prison.
Bill Essayli, the top federal prosecutor in Los Angeles, said that the clerks who didn't comply with the government's demands could face prosecution as well.

加州选举官员对司法部要求扣押“非公民”选票感到沮丧和不安
加利福尼亚州地方选举官员在收到美国司法部的来信后感到沮丧
洛杉矶——加州各地的地方选举官员收到唐纳德·特朗普总统司法部的来信，要求县登记员扣押联邦政府认为在中期选举前发送给非公民选民的选票，这让加州各地的地方选举官员感到困惑和沮丧。
这些信件于周五发出，要求提供大约 20,000 名选民的敏感信息，包括社会安全号码。非公民登记投票或投票是违法的。政府坚称移民投票是全国范围内的一个重大问题，但实际上这种情况相当罕见，甚至连政府自己的调查也表明了这一点。
加州葡萄酒之乡纳帕县的选民登记员约翰·图图尔 (John Tuteur) 表示：“所有这一切只是为了对这次选举的公正性提出巨大质疑。”
司法部周六没有立即回复通过电子邮件发送的置评请求。
图特尔和其他选举官员周六在接受美联社采访时表示，他们已经开始清点该州 2300 万登记选民的选票。
“我们不会改变我们正在做的任何事情。我们正在继续选举，”他说。
联邦政府规定了提供信息的 48 小时期限，并警告说，任何故意统计非公民选票的官员都可能受到法律诉讼。
然而，加州总检察长办公室表示，这些信件存在错误。例如，根据该州法院文件，门多西诺县官员收到了一份非该县居民的名单。
这些信件是中期选举前民主党主导的加州与特朗普司法部之间法律斗争的最新升级。联邦政府于 10 月 15 日（即选举前大约三周）提起诉讼，要求法官禁止该州清点联邦政府认定为可能非公民的人邮寄的选票。由第九巡回上诉法院法官组成的小组将于周日听取有关加州是否可以被迫遵守联邦政府要求的辩论。
图图尔说，周五下午晚些时候，两名身穿制服的国土安全部官员向他的办公室送去了一封信。这封信中包括 42 名被联邦政府指控为非法登记投票的非公民的人的名字。 Tuteur 说，全县超过 13 万人口中，约有 86,000 人登记投票。截至周五，约有 11,000 人已经进行了邮寄选票。在洛杉矶等较大的县，这一数字已超过 331,000 份统计的邮寄选票。
他说，他的员工和亲戚都很担心接下来会发生什么。

body_en: Trump casts his midterm ballot early in Florida - ABC News
Trump casts his midterm ballot early in Florida
President Donald Trump has cast his ballot in the midterm elections, voting for all Republicans in Florida before speaking at a Georgia rally
By JOSH BOAK Associated Press and JILL COLVIN Associated Press
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. -- President Donald Trump cast his ballot in the midterm elections Saturday, saying he voted for all Republicans in Florida before speaking at a Georgia rally.

Trump and first lady Melania Trump arrived at their West Palm Beach polling location at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office together after the president spent the morning at his nearby golf course. Trump has been criticized in the past for voting by mail despite his long history of railing against that method of submitting ballots.
Asked if he voted the party line, Trump, who was wearing an “I Voted” sticker, said, “Very much so.”

Speaking to reporters at the poll site, Trump again defended an ad from Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy . The ad has faced intense blowback for featuring the estranged mother of Democratic rival Dr. Amy Acton, who lost custody of her children after her husband, the children’s stepfather, was indicted for raping Acton when she was 12.

Trump also defended his decision to instruct his administration to file its lawsuit to block certification of the U.S. Senate race in Alaska if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses over the inclusion of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot.
As for the war in Iran, he said, “I may have to finish it off. Or maybe they’ll make a deal, but I’m not sure. Either way, we win.”

Melania Trump , who this week brokered a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the ravaged, Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky so that humanitarian aid could be delivered and civilians evacuated, was asked whether she might travel to Ukraine.

佛罗里达州西棕榈滩——唐纳德·特朗普总统周六在中期选举中投票，他在佐治亚州集会上发表讲话之前表示，他投票给了佛罗里达州的所有共和党人。
总统在附近的高尔夫球场度过了一个上午后，特朗普和第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普一起抵达棕榈滩县选举监督办公室的西棕榈滩投票站。特朗普过去因邮寄投票而受到批评，尽管他长期以来一直反对这种提交选票的方法。

特朗普还为自己的决定进行了辩护，即如果共和党参议员丹·沙利文因将第二位名叫丹·沙利文的候选人纳入选票而失败，他将指示他的政府提起诉讼，阻止阿拉斯加美国参议院竞选的认证。
至于伊朗战争，他说，“我可能必须结束它。或者也许他们会达成协议，但我不确定。无论哪种方式，我们都会赢。”
梅拉尼娅·特朗普本周在被俄罗斯占领的乌克兰城市奥列什基促成了俄罗斯和乌克兰之间的停火，以便能够运送人道主义援助并疏散平民。有人问她是否可能前往乌克兰。

body_en: Man detained at Georgia immigration detention center dies as hunger strike continues
Death inside Folkston facility comes as officials allegedly threaten hunger strikers there with force-feeding

An immigrant detained at a sprawling detention center complex in Georgia died on Friday, local and federal officials confirmed, after the facility has already faced national scrutiny for its response to an ongoing hunger strike inside.

The death inside the D Ray James facility in Folkston, Georgia , comes as federal immigration officials and private contractors are allegedly threatening hunger strikers there with force-feeding, a detained hunger striker, his wife, attorneys and advocates all said this week. Detainees are refusing food to protest prolonged captivity and bad conditions.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) on Saturday confirmed the death inside the facility, which is adjacent to the Folkston ICE processing center. Together, both facilities make up a large detention complex. GEO Group, the private prison company that runs the facilities under contract for the federal government, referred all questions to ICE.

The Georgia bureau of investigation (GBI), a state law enforcement agency, confirmed in an email that the local sheriff’s office requested the GBI conduct an “in-custody death investigation” at the D Ray facility, the Guardian can reveal. ICE and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), its umbrella agency , did not respond to requests for comment about the death or the hunger strike.

“This was a preventable tragedy,” said Azadeh Shahshahani, the legal and advocacy director for Project South, a social justice organization based in Georgia. “We hold ICE and the private prison corporation fully responsible for any harm that migrants suffer at Folkston. We call for an immediate independent investigation into this tragic death and for accountability. Folkston must be shut down immediately.”

The man, Luis Sandoval, was 48 and from El Salvador, ICE said in its statement, adding that at about 1.46am on Friday, facility staff found Sandoval with a ligature around his neck. He was pronounced dead less than an hour later.

Sandoval was arrested by ICE officials earlier this month, and transferred to the Folkston facility on 8 October. In its press release, the agency said Sandoval had prior convictions for aggravated assault and other crimes, and that his death was under investigation.
It was unknown on Saturday whether Sandoval had participated in the hunger strike. The GBI said it could not share more details because of its active investigation.
Sandoval is the 60th person to die in ICE custody since the start of the second Trump administration, as ICE continues with its aggressive anti-immigrant crackdown .

Austin Kocher, president of Relevant Research, which studies the immigration enforcement system, and who is a research fellow at American University, said that this year, there have been an average of one death every 10 days in the custody of ICE. That figure includes people dying in detention centers or in nearby hospitals while still in the custody of ICE.

“Even in the past, there has not been such an overt dehumanization and overt view that migrants’ lives are expendable,” Kocher added. “I worry that that tone [from the Trump administration] has a tendency towards neglect and viewing migrants as disposable.”

Tens of thousands of people have been arrested and detained by ICE, leading to prolonged detention, as immigrants and asylum seekers fight their cases, and the agency has been stepping up its offensive in recent months despite a less showy presence on the streets.
Gone in 90 seconds: an ‘invisibilized’ ICE is arresting more people than ever
One man currently in the Georgia detention center is Andrei Gerdiukov, a Russian asylum seeker who is participating in the hunger strike.

Nearly three weeks ago, Gerdiukov and dozens of others launched a hunger strike to demand their legal cases be processed more quickly through the US immigration system and to protest the conditions of their confinement. The hunger strikers were placed in solitary confinement, according to Gerdiukov and attorneys.

“I feel tired, I feel dizzy. Every move, it is hard,” Gerdiukov said in an interview by phone on Saturday from detention. “They threatened us that they were going to force-feed us.” He had heard about the death but did not know Sandoval.

Gerdiukov and his wife, Polina Chertushkina, came to the US from Russia to seek asylum after they faced persecution for their opposition to the war in Ukraine, Chertushkina said. Their cases are ongoing , but as the couple were driving through Florida this February, they were pulled over and detained by immigration officials. Chertushkina was released, but Gerdiukov was taken to Folkston eight months ago.
“I am so worried about him, I don’t know what to do,” Chertushkina said about the force-feeding threats, speaking on Saturday by phone. Chertushkina is asking lawmakers to assist her husband.
body_zh: 乔治亚州移民拘留中心一名男子因绝食抗议死亡格鲁吉亚 |卫报 跳到主要内容 跳到导航
被拘留在佐治亚州移民拘留中心的一名男子因绝食抗议而死亡
福克斯顿设施内发生死亡事件，据称官员威胁要强制喂食那里的绝食抗议者
当地和联邦官员证实，在佐治亚州一座庞大的拘留中心内，一名被拘留的移民于周五死亡，此前该设施因应对内部持续绝食抗议而面临全国性审查。
一名被拘留的绝食抗议者、他的妻子、律师和支持者本周均表示，佐治亚州福克斯顿的 D Ray James 设施内发生死亡事件，据称联邦移民官员和私人承包商正在用强制喂食来威胁那里的绝食抗议者。被拘留者拒绝食物，以抗议长期监禁和恶劣的条件。
移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 周六证实了该设施内的死亡事件，该设施毗邻 Folkston ICE 处理中心。两个设施共同构成了一个大型拘留所。 GEO 集团是一家私人监狱公司，根据联邦政府合同运营这些设施，该公司将所有问题转交给 ICE。
据《卫报》透露，州执法机构佐治亚州调查局 (GBI) 在一封电子邮件中证实，当地治安官办公室要求 GBI 对 D Ray 设施进行“羁押期间死亡调查”。 ICE 及其保护机构国土安全部 (DHS) 没有回应有关死亡或绝食事件的置评请求。
“这是一场可以避免的悲剧，”佐治亚州社会正义组织“南方计划”的法律和宣传总监阿扎德·沙赫沙哈尼说。 “我们要求 ICE 和私人监狱公司对移民在福克斯顿遭受的任何伤害承担全部责任。我们呼吁立即对这起悲惨死亡事件进行独立调查并追究责任。福克斯顿必须立即关闭。”
ICE 在声明中表示，这名男子名叫路易斯·桑多瓦尔 (Luis Sandoval)，48 岁，来自萨尔瓦多，并补充说，周五凌晨 1 点 46 分左右，设施工作人员发现桑多瓦尔脖子上缠着一根绳子。不到一个小时后，他被宣布死亡。
桑多瓦尔本月早些时候被 ICE 官员逮捕，并于 10 月 8 日被转移到福克斯顿设施。该机构在新闻稿中表示，桑多瓦尔此前曾因严重袭击和其他罪行被定罪，他的死亡正在接受调查。
周六尚不清楚桑多瓦尔是否参加了绝食抗议。 GBI 表示，由于调查正在进行中，因此无法透露更多细节。
桑多瓦尔是自特朗普第二届政府上台以来第 60 名在 ICE 拘留期间死亡的人，同时 ICE 仍在继续严厉的反移民镇压行动。
研究移民执法系统的相关研究公司总裁、美利坚大学研究员奥斯汀·科彻表示，今年，平均每10天就有1人在ICE拘留期间死亡。这一数字包括仍在 ICE 羁押期间在拘留中心或附近医院死亡的人。
科赫补充说：“即使在过去，也没有出现过如此明显的非人化和认为移民的生命是可以牺牲的公开观点。” “我担心（特朗普政府的）这种语气倾向于忽视并将移民视为可抛弃的。”
随着移民和寻求庇护者为案件辩护，数万人被 ICE 逮捕和拘留，导致长期拘留。尽管该机构在街头的表现不那么引人注目，但近几个月来一直在加强攻势。
90 秒内消失：“隐形”ICE 逮捕的人比以往任何时候都多
目前在格鲁吉亚拘留中心的一名男子是参加绝食抗议的俄罗斯寻求庇护者安德烈·格尔迪乌科夫(Andrei Gerdiukov)。
大约三周前，格迪乌科夫和其他数十人发起绝食，要求美国移民系统更快地处理他们的法律案件，并抗议他们的监禁条件。据格尔迪乌科夫和律师称，绝食抗议者被单独监禁。
“我感到疲倦、头晕。每一步都很难，”格尔迪乌科夫周六在被拘留后接受电话采访时说道。 “他们威胁我们要给我们强行喂食。”他听说过桑多瓦尔的死讯，但不认识桑多瓦尔。
切尔图什金娜说，格尔迪乌科夫和他的妻子波琳娜·切尔图什金娜因反对乌克兰战争而受到迫害，从俄罗斯来到美国寻求庇护。他们的案件仍在审理中，但今年二月，当这对夫妇开车穿过佛罗里达州时，他们被移民官员拦下并拘留。 Chertushkina 被释放，但 Gerdiukov 八个月前被带到 Folkston。

title_en: In the Venezuelan stronghold of Doral, some voters discouraged by Trump's policies
title_zh: 在委内瑞拉的据点多拉，一些选民对特朗普的政策感到沮丧
summary: Doral, Florida, has the largest Venezuelan population of any city in the country.
summary_zh: 佛罗里达州多拉尔是委内瑞拉人口最多的城市。
body_en: Latinos voted in record numbers for President Trump in 2024, but polling shows that voting bloc is up for grabs in the midterms.
And one region that reflects that shift is Florida's Miami-Dade County, where Latinos and Hispanics make up more than 70% of the population.
In January, CBS News met Andrea Ramos and her husband in Doral, Florida, as they were celebrating and closely following the capture of former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro.
Ramos, a naturalized U.S. citizen from Venezuela, told CBS News that she credited President Trump with Maduro's capture. Doral has the largest Venezuelan population of any city in the country.
"I had such big admiration for him," Ramos told CBS News about her sentiments for the president following Maduro's arrest and extradition to the U.S.
But about nine months later, her feelings have changed.
"I feel disappointed," Ramos said. "I feel, in a way, betrayed."
While disappointed with the economy, it is the Trump administration's immigration crackdown that has led Ramos to sour on Mr. Trump and the Republican Party.
"Overall, I'm not feeling like the law is being respected," Ramos said.

According to a CBS News Battleground Tracker poll released earlier this month, 60% of Hispanic likely voters said they were likely backing congressional Democrats in the upcoming midterms, compared to 39% who said they were likely backing Republicans.
That marked a considerable shift from 2024 CBS News exit polls, which found that 51% of Hispanics voted for Democrats, compared to 46% who voted for Republicans.
In the same new poll, 59% of Hispanic likely voters found that the Trump administration was trying to deport more people than they had expected, compared to 51% of all likely voters.
Asked in the poll about the Trump administration's focus on deportation, 59% of Hispanic likely voters responded that it was too much, compared to 49% of all likely voters.

Stephanie Caro's family-owned coffee shop in Doral is among many local businesses that have seen a decrease in foot traffic and sales as masked U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents have been photographed on the city's streets.
"I'd say there is a heightened sense of fear," Caro said.
Some local business owners have said they're concerned they'll have to close their doors.
"It really impacts the entire community," Caro said. "People are scared to leave their houses. They're changing their daily routines."
Doral voted for Mr. Trump in 2024, driven by Venezuelan Americans who fled Maduro's socialist regime.

But ICE has increasingly targeted asylum seekers who have pending cases and active work permits, and Mr. Trump's close relationship to Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez has impacted his support in Doral.
When CBS News asked Doral's Republican Mayor Christi Fraga three times if she still supported Mr. Trump, Fraga refused to give a direct answer.
body_zh: 2024 年，拉美裔选民为特朗普总统投票的人数创历史新高，但民意调查显示，投票群体在中期选举中将面临激烈竞争。
反映这一转变的一个地区是佛罗里达州的迈阿密戴德县，该县的拉丁裔和西班牙裔人口占人口的 70% 以上。
一月份，哥伦比亚广播公司新闻在佛罗里达州多拉会见了安德里亚·拉莫斯和她的丈夫，当时他们正在庆祝并密切关注委内瑞拉前领导人尼古拉斯·马杜罗的被捕。
来自委内瑞拉的入籍美国公民拉莫斯告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，她将马杜罗的抓获归功于特朗普总统。多拉是委内瑞拉人口最多的城市。
“我非常钦佩他，”拉莫斯告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，谈到马杜罗被捕并被引渡到美国后她对总统的感受。
但大约九个月后，她的感觉发生了变化。
“我感到失望，”拉莫斯说。 “在某种程度上，我觉得自己被背叛了。”
尽管对经济感到失望，但特朗普政府的移民镇压导致拉莫斯对特朗普和共和党感到不满。
“总的来说，我觉得法律没有得到尊重，”拉莫斯说。
根据本月早些时候发布的哥伦比亚广播公司新闻战场追踪民意调查，60% 的西班牙裔潜在选民表示，他们可能在即将到来的中期选举中支持国会民主党，而 39% 的人表示他们可能支持共和党。
这与 2024 年哥伦比亚广播公司新闻 (CBS News) 出口民意调查相比出现了相当大的转变，该民意调查发现，51% 的拉美裔投票给民主党，而这一比例为 46%。
在同一项新民意调查中，59% 的西班牙裔可能选民发现特朗普政府试图驱逐的人数超出了他们的预期，而所有可能选民中的这一比例为 51%。
在民意调查中，当被问及特朗普政府对驱逐出境的关注时，59% 的西班牙裔可能选民回答说，这太多了，而所有可能选民中的这一比例为 49%。
斯蒂芬妮·卡罗 (Stephanie Caro) 位于多拉尔 (Doral) 的家族经营咖啡店是众多当地企业之一，由于美国移民和海关执法人员蒙面在该市街道上被拍到，客流量和销售额均出现下降。
“我想说，人们的恐惧感更加强烈，”卡罗说。
一些当地企业主表示，他们担心自己将不得不关门。
“这确实影响了整个社区，”卡罗说。 “人们害怕离开家。他们正在改变他们的日常生活。”
在逃离马杜罗社会主义政权的委内瑞拉裔美国人的推动下，多拉尔于 2024 年投票支持特朗普。
但 ICE 越来越多地针对那些有未决案件和有效工作许可证的寻求庇护者，而特朗普与委内瑞拉总统德尔西·罗德里格斯的密切关系影响了他在多拉尔的支持。
当哥伦比亚广播公司新闻三度询问多拉尔市共和党市长克里斯蒂·弗拉加是否仍然支持特朗普时，弗拉加拒绝直接给出答案。

title_en: DOJ demands that some California counties set aside alleged noncitizen ballots
title_zh: 司法部要求加州一些县搁置所谓的非公民选票
summary: Federal prosecutors sent letters to county registrars across California demanding that local officials set aside and verify ballots that the Justice Department said may belong to noncitizens.
summary_zh: 联邦检察官致函加州各地的县登记官，要求地方官员搁置并核实法官 D 所要求的选票。
body_en: Federal prosecutors sent letters to county registrars across California on Friday demanding that local officials set aside and verify ballots that the Justice Department said may belong to noncitizens, according to the Los Angeles County registrar and a letter obtained by The Associated Press.

The letters are the latest escalation in a legal battle between California and President Trump's Justice Department, which has recently focused on the state in its efforts to root out noncitizen voting ahead of the midterm elections . Data shows illegal voting by people who aren't U.S. citizens is incredibly rare, difficult to prove and has not been shown to change the outcome of races.

Earlier this month, the federal government targeted L.A. County and the California Secretary of State's office in a lawsuit that aimed to block them from counting the votes of more than 20,000 people who it alleges are "likely" noncitizen voters. A hearing on the case is scheduled for Tuesday.
The Trump administration on Friday asked the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals to rule on the lawsuit barring a decision from the district judge assigned to the case. They set a deadline for Saturday.

Now, according to the L.A. County registrar's office, at least 18 counties across the state have received similar letters. They were given a 48-hour deadline to provide identifying information corresponding with ballots that the federal government believes were sent to noncitizens illegally registered to vote. The letter requests that county officials also sequester any ballots where citizenship cannot be verified.
"Any election official who knowingly processes the ballot of a noncitizen is opening themselves to legal jeopardy," said First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli.
The Justice Department is asking counties to send information about the voters it suspects are noncitizens including Social Security numbers, ID information, a copy of their registration and more.

That information can help the government and state quickly assess each person suspected of illegally registering to vote, said the letter sent to San Bernardino County voting officials. The letter says the government's list of suspected noncitizen voters includes 1,133 people from the inland Southern California county.

However, the California attorney general's office said the letters contained errors. For example, Mendocino County officials received a list of people who were not residents there, according to a court filing by the state.

Department of Justice spokeswoman Kiersten Pels emphasized in a statement on Saturday that the department is explicitly "not requesting a purge, cancellation of registrations, or any programmatic action."
Instead, Pels wrote, federal officials are asking for collaboration to "ensure the most secure election in California history."

California's secretary of state and the Los Angeles County registrar have opposed the federal government's demands. In legal filings, lawyers for California say the request threatens to delay the certification of the vote and undermine the legitimacy of the November midterms. They have also argued that the federal government's data is unreliable and that their demands risk disenfranchisement of citizens.

Voting is underway in California, with the state's more than 23 million registered voters receiving ballots in the mail earlier this month. The state said in legal filings that over 330,000 mail-in ballots have already been counted.
"All of this is simply meant to raise huge doubts about the integrity of this election," said John Tuteur, the registrar of voters for Napa County in California's wine country.

Tuteur said that two uniformed Department of Homeland Security officers delivered a letter to his office late on Friday afternoon. The letter included the names of 42 people whom the federal government accused of being noncitizens illegally registered to vote. There are roughly 86,000 people registered to vote across the county of over 130,000 people, Tuteur said. Approximately 11,000 people had already cast a mail-in ballot as of Friday.
Tuteur and other election officials who spoke to The Associated Press on Saturday said they have already started to count ballots that have trickled in from the state's 23 million registered voters.
"We're not changing anything we're doing. We're proceeding with the election," he said.
He said his employees and his relatives were worried about what could come next.
"My family's upset, worried about what's going to happen to me," he said.

The letters on Friday came on the heels of a statewide sweep by federal authorities earlier in the week, where 28 people from the list of 20,000 were charged with illegally registering to vote. Some were also charged with illegally voting and lying on naturalization paperwork. Those charges could lead to years in prison.
body_zh: 美国司法部要求加州一些县在 48 小时内搁置并核实所谓的非公民选票 - CBS 新闻
据洛杉矶县登记官和美联社获得的一封信函称，联邦检察官周五致函加州各地的县登记官，要求当地官员搁置并核实司法部称可能属于非公民的选票。
这些信件是加州与特朗普总统司法部之间法律斗争的最新升级，司法部最近重点关注该州在中期选举前根除非公民投票的努力。数据显示，非美国公民的非法投票极其罕见，难以证明，而且尚未被证明可以改变选举结果。
本月早些时候，联邦政府针对洛杉矶县和加州国务卿办公室提起诉讼，旨在阻止他们对 20,000 多名“可能”非公民选民的选民进行计票。该案的听证会定于周二举行。
特朗普政府周五要求第九巡回上诉法院对该诉讼作出裁决，禁止分配给该案的地区法官做出裁决。他们设定了周六的最后期限。
据洛杉矶县登记办公室称，目前全州至少有 18 个县收到了类似的信件。他们被要求在 48 小时内提供与选票相对应的识别信息，联邦政府认为这些信息是发送给非法登记投票的非公民的。这封信要求县官员还扣押无法核实公民身份的所有选票。
美国检察官第一助理比尔·埃萨利表示：“任何故意处理非公民选票的选举官员都会面临法律危险。”
司法部要求各县发送其怀疑为非公民的选民的信息，包括社会安全号码、身份证信息、登记副本等。
发给圣贝纳迪诺县投票官员的信称，这些信息可以帮助政府和州快速评估涉嫌非法登记投票的每个人。信中称，政府的可疑非公民选民名单中包括来自南加州内陆县的 1,133 人。
加州国务卿和洛杉矶县登记官反对联邦政府的要求。加州律师在法律文件中表示，这一要求可能会推迟投票认证，并损害 11 月中期选举的合法性。他们还认为联邦政府的数据不可靠，他们的要求可能会剥夺公民的公民权。
加利福尼亚州的投票正在进行中，该州超过 2300 万登记选民本月早些时候收到了邮寄选票。该州在法律文件中表示，已经统计了超过 33 万张邮寄选票。
周五发出这些信件之前，联邦当局本周早些时候在全州范围内进行了扫荡，20,000 人名单中的 28 人被指控非法登记投票。有些人还被指控非法投票和在入籍文件上撒谎。这些指控可能导致数年监禁。
司法部民权部门已提起 31 起诉讼，试图迫使各州交出未经编辑的选民名册副本。该部门曾表示，希望确保各州保持干净的选民名单，但后来又承认，它还打算与国土安全部共享数据，以便筛选名单中的非公民。
民权部门助理总检察长哈米特·迪隆 (Harmeet Dhillon) 7 月份向所有 50 个州发出信函，威胁称，如果这些州故意允许非公民留在选民名册上，我们将采取刑事行动。
到目前为止，司法部已经输掉了其中 26 起案件，并且尚未取得任何法律胜利。

title_en: Facing an electoral wipeout, Trump goes after the system
title_zh: 特朗普让阿拉斯加成为他争夺选举权力的最新前沿
summary: The move by the Justice Department to try and preemptively block Alaska’s Senate results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses stunned officials in both parties.
summary_zh: 如果共和党参议员丹·沙利文在博茨瓦纳选举中落败，司法部将试图先发制人地阻止阿拉斯加州参议院的选举结果，这让官员们感到震惊
body_en: President Donald Trump is escalating his crusade to exert control of America’s elections as his party barrels towards a potentially bruising midterm.

The Justice Department has already filed lawsuits in nearly every state to try and gain access to voter files. Trump revisited his longstanding bid to restrict mail voting, sparking a legal battle that reached the Supreme Court. He sought to make anti-terrorism funds for state and local governments contingent on how they administer elections. He has threatened to withhold federal election funding from states that refuse to change voter registration forms and sparred with Republican lawmakers over a bill to overhaul elections.

But with most of those efforts stalling, on Thursday, just 12 days before Election Day, the DOJ took things even further: In an extraordinary move, it asked a court to preemptively block Alaska’s Senate results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses, stunning current and former election officials in both parties.

“Boy, they are scraping the bottom of the barrel. It feels like a real desperation play to me, because it has got zero basis in the law,” said Ben Ginsberg, a veteran Republican election law expert who was counsel to George W. Bush’s 2000 and 2004 presidential campaigns.

At virtually every corner, courts have rebuffed Trump’s efforts, and legal experts expect the latest DOJ maneuver to have the same outcome. The requests for voter rolls were blocked repeatedly by members of Trump’s own party and struck down in court . The attempt to restrict mail voting was ultimately blocked by the Supreme Court. Federal judges blocked both the anti-terrorism and election funding efforts. The SAVE Act, which would require voters to provide proof of citizenship at the polls, has stalled in the Senate.
But Trump keeps pushing, telling reporters Friday that he had personally green-lit the Alaska lawsuit: “I'm the one that said 'Do it.’”
The gambit is another sign that Trump is once again ramping up his efforts to exert greater control over how elections are administered — with officials bracing for what may come next.

“I think there is an attempt to lay a foundation to say, ‘If we had won these lawsuits, we would have won the election,’” Gabriel Sterling, a Republican and former senior Georgia elections official who sparred with Trump over his false claims of fraud in the state in 2020, said of the Alaska lawsuit. “So, for them, filing and losing for them is the same difference, tactically speaking, potentially.”

Trump has been claiming elections were being stolen from him since the 2016 primaries , and his wide-ranging legal and political attempts to overturn his 2020 election loss sparked a riot at the U.S. Capitol in January 2021, even as some in his party want him to move on .

“The federal government is his company, and he gets to call all the shots of his company, and that's just never how it's been done before,” said Stephen Richer, Maricopa County, Arizona’s former GOP chief election official.

POLITICO reached out to the offices of every Republican statewide election official in America for a response to the DOJ’s action in Alaska. Four declined to comment, and the rest did not respond. Their silence shows just how powerful Trump remains in the party, and how few are willing to cross him just days before November’s midterms.

"The survival rate politically of people who oppose Donald Trump on this issue is not great if you're Republican,” said Richer, who was ousted by a more conservative Republican in a 2024 primary after defending the county’s 2020 election results against a yearslong campaign from Trump and his allies to try to prove they were rigged .
Arizona Democratic Secretary of State Adrian Fontes railed against the DOJ’s lawsuit, accusing the department of “working as the president's lawyers.”

“The Department of Justice is acting in a monstrously political way, and it's purely inappropriate, and they lose a lot of credibility by putting their thumb on the scales,” Fontes said in an interview Friday afternoon. “This attempt in Alaska, if it comes to Arizona, will also fail.”

The Justice Department, in a statement posted on social media , said "claims that DOJ is trying to stop Alaska’s election are FALSE." Instead, the DOJ argued it was "seeking to protect election integrity, consistent with the National Voter Registration Act (enacted by Congress) and ensure the will of Alaska voters is respected."

Washington state Attorney General Nick Brown, a Democrat, described the legal filing in Alaska as “part of a concerted effort to control the election and to try to dictate the outcome in Donald Trump and the Republican Party’s favor.”
Brown said he worried the administration would contest the results of the midterms.

“That is not hypothetical,” Brown said. “This is what the president has done for years now, and he has the entire power of government, and most importantly, the Department of Justice around elections, acting at his request.”
Sterling predicted the effort would backfire on the GOP.

“By talking about stolen elections, by talking about cheating, they're suppressing their own vote and they're encouraging the votes of their opponents,” he said. “So tactically, I think it's politically moronic.”
body_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统正在升级他的十字军东征，以控制美国的选举，因为他的政党正朝着可能惨烈的中期选举迈进。
司法部已经在几乎每个州提起诉讼，试图获取选民档案。特朗普重新审视了他长期以来限制邮寄投票的主张，引发了一场法律战，并闹到了最高法院。他试图根据州和地方政府管理选举的方式为其提供反恐资金。他威胁要扣留那些拒绝改变选民登记表格的州的联邦选举资金，并与共和党议员就一项改革选举的法案发生争执。
但随着大部分努力陷入停滞，周四，距离选举日仅 12 天，美国司法部采取了更进一步的措施：采取一项非同寻常的举措，要求法院在共和党参议员丹·沙利文 (Dan Sullivan) 失败的情况下，先发制人地阻止阿拉斯加州参议院的选举结果，这令两党现任和前任选举官员感到震惊。
“天哪，他们正在彻底解决问题。对我来说，这真是一场绝望的游戏，因为它的法律基础为零，”曾担任乔治·W·布什 (George W. Bush) 2000 年和 2004 年总统竞选顾问的资深共和党选举法专家本·金斯伯格 (Ben Ginsberg) 说。
几乎在每个角落，法院都拒绝了特朗普的努力，法律专家预计司法部的最新举措也会产生同样的结果。选民登记的请求多次遭到特朗普所在政党成员的阻止，并在法庭上被驳回。限制邮寄投票的尝试最终被最高法院阻止。联邦法官阻止了反恐和选举资助工作。 《SAVE 法案》要求选民在投票时提供公民身份证明，但该法案在参议院陷入僵局。
但特朗普继续推动，周五告诉记者，他亲自为阿拉斯加诉讼开了绿灯：“我是那个说‘做吧’的人。”
这一策略是特朗普再次加大力度对选举管理方式施加更大控制的另一个迹象——官员们正在为接下来可能发生的事情做好准备。
“我认为有人试图奠定基础，‘如果我们赢得了这些诉讼，我们就会赢得选举’，”共和党人、前佐治亚州选举高级官员加布里埃尔·斯特林(Gabriel Sterling)在谈到阿拉斯加诉讼时表示，他曾因特朗普在2020年谎称该州存在欺诈行为而与特朗普发生过争执。 “因此，对他们来说，从战术上讲，申请和失败可能是相同的区别。”
自 2016 年初选以来，特朗普一直声称选举权被窃取，他为推翻 2020 年选举失利而进行的广泛法律和政治尝试引发了 2021 年 1 月美国国会大厦的骚乱，尽管他的党内一些人希望他继续前进。
亚利桑那州马里科帕县前共和党首席选举官员斯蒂芬·里彻 (Stephen Richer) 表示：“联邦政府是他的公司，他可以对公司做所有决定，以前从未这样做过。”
《政治》杂志联系了美国每一位共和党全州选举官员的办公室，寻求对司法部在阿拉斯加州的行动的回应。其中四家拒绝置评，其余则没有回应。他们的沉默表明特朗普在党内的影响力有多大，以及在 11 月中期选举前几天愿意反对他的人有多么少。
里彻说：“如果你是共和党人，在这个问题上反对唐纳德·特朗普的人在政治上的生存率并不高。”里彻为该县 2020 年的选举结果辩护，反对特朗普及其盟友长达数年的竞选活动，试图证明他们被操纵，之后在 2024 年的初选中被更为保守的共和党人赶下台。
亚利桑那州民主党国务卿阿德里安·丰特斯强烈反对司法部的诉讼，指责该部门“充当总统的律师”。
丰特斯在周五下午接受采访时表示：“司法部的行为方式极其政治化，这完全是不恰当的，他们因为把拇指放在天平上而失去了很多可信度。” “阿拉斯加的这次尝试，如果涉及到亚利桑那州，也会失败。”
司法部在社交媒体上发布的一份声明中表示，“有关司法部试图阻止阿拉斯加选举的说法是错误的。”相反，司法部辩称，它“寻求保护选举的完整性，符合《国家选民登记法》（由国会颁布），并确保阿拉斯加选民的意愿得到尊重。”
华盛顿州司法部长、民主党人尼克·布朗将阿拉斯加的法律申请描述为“控制选举并试图以对唐纳德·特朗普和共和党有利的方式决定结果的共同努力的一部分”。
布朗表示，他担心政府会对中期选举的结果提出异议。
“这不是假设，”布朗说。 “这就是总统多年来所做的事情，他拥有政府的全部权力，最重要的是，司法部在选举方面按照他的要求行事。”
斯特林预测，这一努力将对共和党产生适得其反的效果。
“通过谈论选举被盗，通过谈论作弊，他们正在压制自己的选票，并鼓励对手的选票，”他说。 “所以从战术上讲，我认为这在政治上是愚蠢的。”

summary: Critics decry Trump administration rule that lets hunters lure bears with human foods on federal lands in Alaska A new Trump administration rule allows hunters to bait bears on federal lands in Alaska with bacon, doughnuts, meat scraps or other human foods typ

body_en: New Trump rule allows hunters to bait bears in Alaska with doughnuts, bacon and more | Trump administration
New Trump rule allows hunters to bait bears in Alaska with doughnuts, bacon and more
Critics decry Trump administration rule that lets hunters lure bears with human foods on federal lands in Alaska

A new Trump administration rule allows hunters to bait bears on federal lands in Alaska with bacon, doughnuts, meat scraps or other human foods typically used to help kill the trophy animals at close range.

Opponents say the practice will cause bears to be more aggressive around humans, and allege that the rule change is a political gift to largely rightwing trophy hunters. The rule replaces a 2024 Biden administration rule that banned the practice, and environmental groups criticized the move as “indefensible and inexcusable”.

“We are discouraged to see this rule come back, specifically the bear baiting piece which is cruel and dangerous, not only to wildlife but the public as well,” said Drew Robertson, senior regulatory specialist for Humane World for Animals .

The US interior department on Friday published the rule on the federal register, and it will take effect in mid-November. It marks the latest in a series of rule changes at the state and federal levels since 2023 that allow trophy hunters to use what critics say are barbaric and unethical practices to kill animals.

Doug Burgum, the secretary of the interior, wrote in a press release that the latest rule was developed in response to demands by Alaska residents and it was a “commonsense framework and gives Alaskans a stronger voice in decisions affecting the lands, wildlife and traditions they know best”.

The federal rule does not list specific foods that are allowed, but it defers to state rules, which allow for baiting, and hunters typically use “the cheapest and most effective food, which is high fat and high sugar”, said Nicholas Arrivo, a managing attorney at Animal Protection Law. Hunters typically put food in a steel drum or garbage can, monitor the bait, then set up from a nearby blind from which they kill the bear at short range, Arrivo said.
The practice raises broader ethical questions around the spirit and intent of sport hunting.
“It is a more extreme practice than the hunting traditions that people think of, and many hunters would not see this as a fair chase,” Robertson said.

The move comes after Alaska and federal officials in recent years started allowing sport hunters to hunt big game with controversial practices, like shooting bears from helicopters, shooting swimming caribou from motor boats, killing wolf pups in their dens and using artificial lights to draw bears out of the dens to kill them. The bear baiting is not highly unusual as about a dozen states allow similar practices, but more do not.
The rule change came at the direction of Donald Trump in an executive order , called Unleashing Alaska’s Extraordinary Resource Potential, which was issued in his second administration’s early days.

“It was a priority for the president … and he included direction to reissue this rule, which says that there is a political motivation, not something that seems to be derived from careful consideration,” Robertson said.

This baiting rule has a long history. A ban was first put in place by Barack Obama’s administration, then undone by the first Trump administration. Litigation upheld the Obama rule and overturned the Trump rule. The Biden administration then reimplemented the rule in 2024, largely because science shows that the practice will make bears more aggressive, and put park visitors’ lives at risk.

Though the Trump administration has said the rule was designed to give the state more control over the land, the lands are federal and Congress created the federal land program to give the federal government decision-making power, not state governments, Arrivo said. He said it “is anathema to federal land management goals … of preserving wildlife diversity”.

Though no decision has yet been made about a lawsuit, Arrivo said the interior department’s decision to fully scrap the 2024 rule that underwent a more robust scientific process “doesn’t smell right and raises questions about the legality of this rule”.
body_zh: 特朗普新规定允许猎人在阿拉斯加用甜甜圈、培根等引诱熊特朗普政府 |卫报 跳到主要内容 跳到导航
特朗普新规定允许猎人在阿拉斯加用甜甜圈、培根等引诱熊
批评者谴责特朗普政府允许猎人在阿拉斯加联邦土地上用人类食物引诱熊的规定
特朗普政府的一项新规定允许猎人在阿拉斯加的联邦土地上用培根、甜甜圈、肉渣或其他通常用于近距离杀死战利品动物的人类食物来引诱熊。
反对者表示，这种做法将导致熊对人类更具攻击性，并声称规则的改变对大多数右翼战利品猎人来说是一份政治礼物。该规则取代了 2024 年拜登政府禁止这种做法的规则，环保组织批评此举“站不住脚、不可原谅”。
人道动物世界高级监管专家德鲁·罗伯逊 (Drew Robertson) 表示：“看到这条规则重新出现，我们感到很沮丧，特别是捕熊的行为，不仅对野生动物而且对公众来说都是残酷和危险的。”
美国内政部周五在联邦公报上公布了这一规定，并将于 11 月中旬生效。这是自 2023 年以来州和联邦层面一系列规则变化中的最新一项，这些规则允许战利品猎人使用批评者所说的野蛮和不道德的做法来杀死动物。
内政部长道格·布尔古姆在一份新闻稿中写道，最新规则是根据阿拉斯加居民的要求制定的，它是一个“常识性框架，让阿拉斯加人在影响他们最了解的土地、野生动物和传统的决策中拥有更强的发言权”。
动物保护法的管理律师尼古拉斯·阿里沃（Nicholas Arrivo）表示，联邦规定没有列出允许的具体食物，但它遵循州规定，允许使用诱饵，猎人通常使用“最便宜、最有效的食物，即高脂肪和高糖”。阿里沃说，猎人通常将食物放入钢桶或垃圾桶中，监控诱饵，然后在附近的百叶窗上设置诱饵，在近距离杀死熊。
这种做法引发了围绕运动狩猎的精神和意图的更广泛的道德问题。
“这是一种比人们想象的狩猎传统更为极端的做法，许多猎人不会认为这是一次公平的追逐，”罗伯逊说。
在此之前，阿拉斯加和联邦官员近年来开始允许运动狩猎者使用有争议的做法来狩猎大型动物，例如从直升机上射杀熊，从摩托艇上射杀游泳的驯鹿，在狼穴中杀死狼崽，以及使用人造光将熊从狼穴中吸引出来杀死它们。诱熊事件并不罕见，大约有十几个州允许类似的做法，但更多州则不允许。
这一规则的改变是在唐纳德·特朗普的一项行政命令的指导下进行的，该命令名为“释放阿拉斯加的非凡资源潜力”，该命令是在他的第二届政府初期发布的。
罗伯逊说：“这是总统的首要任务……他包括重新发布这条规则的指示，该规则表明存在政治动机，而不是经过仔细考虑而得出的东西。”
这种诱饵规则有着悠久的历史。巴拉克·奥巴马政府首先实施了一项禁令，然后被特朗普第一届政府撤销。诉讼维持了奥巴马的规则并推翻了特朗普的规则。拜登政府随后在 2024 年重新实施了这一规定，主要是因为科学表明，这种做法会让熊变得更具攻击性，并使公园游客的生命面临危险。
阿里沃说，尽管特朗普政府表示，该规则的目的是让州对土地有更多的控制权，但土地是联邦的，国会制定联邦土地计划是为了赋予联邦政府决策权，而不是州政府。他表示，这“违背了保护野生动物多样性的联邦土地管理目标……”。
尽管尚未就诉讼做出决定，但阿里沃表示，内政部决定完全废除经过更严格的科学程序的 2024 年规则，“听起来不太对劲，并引发了人们对该规则合法性的质疑”。

Trump casts his midterm ballot early in Florida
WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — President Donald Trump cast his ballot in the midterm elections Saturday, saying he voted for all Republicans in Florida before speaking at a Georgia rally.
WATCH: Trump says he ordered suit to block Alaska Senate results if GOP loses

Trump and first lady Melania Trump arrived at their West Palm Beach polling location at the Palm Beach County Supervisor of Elections office together after the president spent the morning at his nearby golf course. Trump has been criticized in the past for voting by mail despite his long history of railing against that method of submitting ballots.
Asked if he voted the party line, Trump, who was wearing an "I Voted" sticker, said, "Very much so."

Speaking to reporters at the poll site, Trump again defended an ad from Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. The ad has faced intense blowback for featuring the estranged mother of Democratic rival Dr. Amy Acton, who lost custody of her children after her husband, the children's stepfather, was indicted for raping Acton when she was 12.

Trump also defended his decision to instruct his administration to file its lawsuit to block certification of the U.S. Senate race in Alaska if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses over the inclusion of a second candidate named Dan Sullivan on the ballot.
As for the war in Iran, he said, "I may have to finish it off. Or maybe they'll make a deal, but I'm not sure. Either way, we win."

Melania Trump, who this week brokered a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the ravaged, Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky so that humanitarian aid could be delivered and civilians evacuated, was asked whether she might travel to Ukraine.
In Florida, Trump has endorsed Republican Rep. Byron Donalds, who is running against David Jolly, a Republican-turned-independent-turned-Democrat, to succeed term-limited Gov. Ron DeSantis.

He has also campaigned for Republican Sen. Ashley Moody, who is running to fill the last two years of Secretary of State Marco Rubio's former Senate term against progressive state lawmaker Angie Nixon.

观看：特朗普表示，如果共和党失败，他将下令提起诉讼，阻止阿拉斯加州参议院的结果
总统在附近的高尔夫球场度过了一个上午后，特朗普和第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普一起抵达棕榈滩县选举监督办公室的西棕榈滩投票站。特朗普过去因邮寄投票而受到批评，尽管他长期以来一直反对这种提交选票的方法。
当被问及是否投票支持党派路线时，戴着“我投票”贴纸的特朗普说：“非常喜欢。”
特朗普在投票站对记者发表讲话，再次为俄亥俄州共和党州长候选人维韦克·拉马斯瓦米的广告辩护。该广告因以民主党竞争对手艾米·阿克顿博士的分居母亲为主角而面临强烈反弹。艾米·阿克顿博士的丈夫，即孩子们的继父，因在她 12 岁时强奸阿克顿而被起诉，从而失去了孩子们的监护权。
特朗普还为自己的决定进行了辩护，即如果共和党参议员丹·沙利文因将第二位名叫丹·沙利文的候选人纳入选票而失败，他将指示他的政府提起诉讼，阻止阿拉斯加美国参议院竞选的认证。

梅拉尼娅·特朗普本周在被俄罗斯占领的乌克兰城市奥列什基促成了俄罗斯和乌克兰之间的停火，以便能够运送人道主义援助并疏散平民。有人问她是否可能前往乌克兰。

title_en: Trade tariffs cause whiplash at Port Milwaukee
title_zh: 贸易关税导致密尔沃基港遭受重创
summary: Sacha Pfeiffer visits Port Milwaukee to see how President Trump's tariffs have affected the flow of goods and impacted the regional economy.
summary_zh: 萨莎·菲佛 (Sacha Pfeiffer) 访问密尔沃基港，了解特朗普总统的关税如何影响货物流动和地区经济。
body_en: Trade tariffs cause whiplash at Port Milwaukee : NPR
Trade tariffs cause whiplash at Port Milwaukee Sacha Pfeiffer visits Port Milwaukee to see how President Trump's tariffs have affected the flow of goods and impacted the regional economy.
Trade tariffs cause whiplash at Port Milwaukee
Sacha Pfeiffer visits Port Milwaukee to see how President Trump's tariffs have affected the flow of goods and impacted the regional economy.

As we heard from those early voters in Texas and from coverage of the protests in France, the economy and affordability are surging concerns globally. It's also a concern locally in Milwaukee, where I'm hosting this program tonight. If you look at a map, you realize the city is located on a massive superhighway of water. Milwaukee is on Lake Michigan, part of the Great Lakes region, and that region is its own economy. Cargo from around the world is shipped across the Great Lakes, and all that maritime trade contributes to a regional economy worth about $9 trillion.

Now look at that map again. Four of the five great lakes are shared between the United States and Canada. Those two countries are now in an economic battle due to President Trump's tariffs, and that fight is harming port cities like Milwaukee. That is why I found myself this week on a long concrete pier on the port of Milwaukee, overlooking the vast expanse of Lake Michigan and talking with port director Benji Timm.
BENJI TIMM: So the boat is coming from the East. You can see the breakwater. There's a break in the breakwater out there. And there's...
PFEIFFER: A little passage for boats to get through. Yeah.

TIMM: Yes, between the light - the two lighthouses. That's where the vessels would come in. And if they're going into our inner mooring basin, they'd pass underneath the Hoan Bridge in the highway. If they're coming into one of our terminals here, they'd come straight in into one of these slips.
PFEIFFER: So whether they're coming from Canada or Europe, that is the way they get in.
PFEIFFER: Port Milwaukee does business with more than 300 ships a year that import goods from all over.

TIMM: So there are steel beams on the terminal, and this steel came in from Luxembourg. It came in for a hospital project from Minnesota. It's unloaded from a vessel here, and then it's loaded up onto trucks and then trucked over to Minnesota.
PFEIFFER: Can we not make this in the United States?
TIMM: That was a special gauge of steel, I know.
PFEIFFER: I mean, and is that partly what the Trump administration hopes for eventually, is that we can make this steel at home? And by these tariffs, we won't have to bring it in from Europe?
TIMM: That's the idea, yeah, is that we increase our production here. And again, I don't think anybody would argue with that, but we have to put the components into place to get us to that point.

PFEIFFER: Over the past year, Timm watched anxiously as the Trump administration added or threatened tariffs on all sorts of items - steel, auto parts, salt, agricultural commodities, timber. The tariffs could come at any time, and that affects the budgets and supply chains of countless companies that rely on this port.
What is your distress level about the impact that tariffs are having on the Milwaukee economy?

TIMM: It's kind of whiplash. You know, it's - it has not been consistent. When the administration makes an announcement, we listen very closely, and then we try and figure out how it'll affect us. We try not to freak out because oftentimes it'll change.
body_zh: 贸易关税导致密尔沃基港遭受重创：NPR
贸易关税在密尔沃基港引发猛烈攻击 萨沙·菲佛 (Sacha Pfeiffer) 访问密尔沃基港，了解特朗普总统的关税如何影响货物流动和地区经济。
贸易关税导致密尔沃基港遭受重创
萨莎·菲佛 (Sacha Pfeiffer) 访问密尔沃基港，了解特朗普总统的关税如何影响货物流动和地区经济。
正如我们从德克萨斯州早期选民和法国抗议活动的报道中听到的那样，经济和负担能力正在全球范围内引发担忧。这也是密尔沃基当地的一个问题，我今晚将在那里主持这个节目。如果你看一下地图，你就会发现这座城市位于一条巨大的水上高速公路上。密尔沃基位于密歇根湖畔，是五大湖区的一部分，该地区是它自己的经济体。来自世界各地的货物通过五大湖运输，所有海上贸易为价值约 9 万亿美元的区域经济做出了贡献。
现在再看看那张地图。五个大湖中有四个是美国和加拿大共有的。由于特朗普总统的关税，这两个国家现在正处于一场经济斗争中，这场斗争正在损害密尔沃基等港口城市。这就是为什么我本周在密尔沃基港的一个长长的混凝土码头上，俯瞰着广阔的密歇根湖，并与港口总监本吉·蒂姆交谈。
BENJI TIMM：所以船是从东方来的。你可以看到防波堤。那里的防波堤有一个缺口。还有...
PFEIFFER：供船只通过的小通道。是的。
蒂姆：是的，在光之间——两座灯塔。这就是船只进入的地方。如果它们要进入我们的内部系泊池，它们会从高速公路上的还安桥下面经过。如果他们进入我们这里的任一航站楼，他们就会直接进入这些单张之一。
PFEIFFER：所以无论他们来自加拿大还是欧洲，这都是他们进入的方式。
PFEIFFER：密尔沃基港每年与 300 多艘从各地进口货物的船只进行业务往来。
蒂姆：航站楼上有钢梁，这些钢来自卢森堡。它来自明尼苏达州的一个医院项目。它从这里的船上卸下，然后装上卡车，然后用卡车运到明尼苏达州。
PFEIFFER：我们不能在美国做这个吗？
蒂姆：我知道那是一种特殊规格的钢材。
普法伊弗：我的意思是，这也是特朗普政府最终希望的部分内容吗？我们可以在国内生产这种钢材吗？通过这些关税，我们就不必从欧洲进口了？
蒂姆：是的，这就是我们增加产量的想法。再说一遍，我认为没有人会反对这一点，但我们必须将各个组成部分落实到位才能实现这一目标。
普法伊弗：在过去的一年里，蒂姆焦急地看着特朗普政府对各种商品增加或威胁征收关税——钢铁、汽车零部件、盐、农产品、木材。关税可能随时发生，这会影响依赖该港口的无数公司的预算和供应链。
您对关税对密尔沃基经济影响的担忧程度如何？
蒂姆：有点像鞭打。你知道，它并不一致。当政府发布公告时，我们会非常仔细地倾听，然后尝试弄清楚它将如何影响我们。我们尽量不要惊慌，因为事情常常会发生变化。

title_en: Russia steps up election influence efforts in final stretch of midterms
title_zh: 俄罗斯在中期选举最后阶段加强选举影响力
summary: Researchers who track online influence operations say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U.S. and around the world.
summary_zh: 追踪在线影响力运作的研究人员表示，克里姆林宫支持的团体正在更新他们在之前用来散布不信任和不和的策略。
body_en: Russia steps up election influence efforts ahead of midterms : NPR

Russia steps up election influence efforts ahead of midterms Researchers who track online influence operations say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U.S. and around the world.
Russia steps up election influence efforts in final stretch of midterms

A pedestrian looks at his smartphone on an embankment with the Kremlin in the background in central Moscow on Oct. 8, 2026. Researchers who track online influence operations say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U.S. and around the world. Igor Ivanko/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

Russian operatives are pumping out fabricated claims about Democratic candidates, AI-manipulated videos of celebrities and fake posts impersonating real news outlets in an effort to influence American voters in the final run-up to Election Day.

Researchers who track online influence operations and lawmakers who've been briefed by the intelligence community say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing familiar tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U.S. and around the world.
Top 2 Democrats on Intel say they're preparing for Trump to claim foreign meddling

"It's a carnival out there," Rep. Jim Himes of Connecticut , the ranking member on the House intelligence committee, told reporters this week. "They're throwing everything out there to generate a sense of chaos and anarchy."
The goal is to exacerbate divisions, erode confidence in democracy and, crucially, undermine U.S. support for Ukraine.

"At the end of the day, the main issue for Russia is and has to be Ukraine," said Darren Linvill, co-director of Clemson University's Media Forensics Hub, who has tracked foreign propaganda campaigns for years.

Linvill says the Russian playbook is consistent. A false claim or divisive narrative is seeded on social media or on a fake website posing as a news organization or think tank. It's spread by state media, automated fake accounts or, increasingly, paid influencers, in the hopes that it gets seen and repeated by real people.

"In the same way that marketing companies will pay an influencer to disseminate, you know, 'Nike's a great shoe,' the Russians do it with false information and made-up lies," he said. "They use influencers that know their audience, that are part of that audience, and they know how to give that audience a message that they want to hear," Linvill said.
A Russian operation put that playbook to work this week to spread a baseless accusation against a Democratic U.S. Senate candidate.

Linvill and several other research groups attributed them to Russian operators the research community has dubbed Storm-1516 . It's known for staging fake videos with actors and laundering their claims through influencer accounts with large followings.

Two fraudulent videos targeting the Senate candidate were posted on Tuesday on X by an account created last month that had few followers. The account's X profile said it was based in the U.S. but the social media platform publicly flagged it as possibly using a proxy such as a virtual private network, which could disguise its location.
OpenAI caught Russians and Iranians using ChatGPT for influence campaigns

The videos were likely created using artificial intelligence, according to Graphika, a research company that analyzes online communities. Linvill said a hallmark of Storm-1516 videos is the use of real actors whose faces are swapped using AI to look like someone else.

The post was immediately shared by a network of 15 accounts Linvill flagged as bots. About 12 hours later, one of the videos was shared in new posts by three X accounts with large followings, which researchers said have previously amplified other narratives attributed to Storm-1516. One of them has solicited paid partnerships on X. Soon other X accounts began resharing the large accounts' posts in replies to politicians and journalists.

One of the two fake videos racked up roughly 857,000 views within 24 hours, according to an analysis by Alethea, a threat intelligence company. By late on Wednesday, the account that first posted the videos and one of the large accounts that reshared the claim had been suspended by X, and the two other large accounts that amplified it had taken down their posts.

In the run-up to the 2024 presidential election, Storm-1516 posted fraudulent videos making similar unfounded accusations against Democratic vice presidential nominee Tim Walz and purporting to show ballots for President Trump being torn up .

俄罗斯特工正在散布有关民主党候选人的捏造言论、人工智能操纵的名人视频以及冒充真实新闻媒体的虚假帖子，以期在选举日的最后一刻影响美国选民。
追踪在线影响力运作的研究人员和听取情报界通报的立法者表示，克里姆林宫支持的组织正在更新他们在美国和世界各地以前的选举中用来散布不信任和不和的熟悉策略。
英特尔的两名顶级民主党人表示，他们正在为特朗普声称外国干预做准备
“这是一场狂欢节，”众议院情报委员会高级成员、康涅狄格州众议员吉姆·海姆斯本周对记者说。 “他们把一切都扔在那里，以产生混乱和无政府状态的感觉。”
其目标是加剧分歧，削弱对民主的信心，最重要的是，削弱美国对乌克兰的支持。
“归根结底，俄罗斯的主要问题是而且必须是乌克兰，”多年来一直跟踪外国宣传活动的克莱姆森大学媒体取证中心联席主任达伦·林维尔说。
林维尔表示，俄罗斯的战术是一致的。虚假主张或分裂性叙述散布在社交媒体或冒充新闻机构或智囊团的虚假网站上。它通过官方媒体、自动虚假账户或越来越多的付费影响者传播，希望它能被真实的人看到和重复。
“就像营销公司花钱请有影响力的人来传播‘耐克是一双很棒的鞋’一样，俄罗斯人也用虚假信息和编造的谎言来传播，”他说。林维尔说：“他们使用的影响者了解他们的受众，他们是受众的一部分，他们知道如何向受众传达他们想听到的信息。”
俄罗斯的一项行动本周将这一策略付诸实施，散布针对美国民主党参议员候选人的毫无根据的指控。
林维尔和其他几个研究小组将它们归因于俄罗斯运营商，研究界将其称为 Storm-1516。它以与演员一起制作虚假视频并通过拥有大量粉丝的影响者帐户洗钱而闻名。
周二，一个上个月创建的账户在 X 上发布了两段针对参议院候选人的欺诈视频，该账户的粉丝很少。该帐户的 X 个人资料称其总部位于美国，但该社交媒体平台公开标记其可能使用虚拟专用网络等代理，这可能会掩盖其位置。
OpenAI 发现俄罗斯人和伊朗人使用 ChatGPT 进行影响力活动
根据分析在线社区的研究公司 Graphika 的说法，这些视频很可能是使用人工智能创建的。 Linvill 表示，Storm-1516 视频的一个特点是使用真实演员，他们的面孔通过人工智能交换，看起来像其他人。

title_en: Republican billionaire Rick Jackson is walking a Trump tightrope in his quest to lead Georgia
title_zh: 共和党亿万富翁里克·杰克逊在寻求领导佐治亚州时正在走钢丝。
summary: Rick Jackson wants to be Georgia's governor and the Republican billionaire is promising to fight for working-class voters
summary_zh: 里克·杰克逊希望成为佐治亚州州长，共和党亿万富翁承诺为工人阶级选民而战
body_en: Republican billionaire Rick Jackson is walking a Trump tightrope in his quest to lead Georgia - ABC News
Republican billionaire Rick Jackson is walking a Trump tightrope in his quest to lead Georgia
Rick Jackson wants to be Georgia's governor and the Republican billionaire is promising to fight for working-class voters

ATLANTA -- He's hardly the first billionaire to promise working-class voters he'll fight for them in public office. Rick Jackson , the Republican candidate for Georgia governor, has even compared himself to the real estate mogul who reached the Oval Office.

But Jackson’s path differs from Donald Trump’s , and the 72-year-old healthcare magnate and investor brings a vastly different persona to his first campaign. Unlike Trump, who was born to wealth , Jackson spent his early years bouncing through foster homes before launching his first company as a young man.

Now, he wants to leverage both his similarities and contrasts with the president, a challenge he's tackling with buckets of his own campaign cash and a personal story that anchors his appeal to voters.
“I have lived in poverty,” Jackson says. “When you have not eaten, you never forget that, and you don’t forget the people that are struggling.”

Democratic nominee Keisha Lance Bottoms , a former Atlanta mayor, disputes Jackson’s altruistic pitch, setting up the Nov. 3 election as a test of whether an alternate, softer version of conservative billionaire politics can complement or even counter Trump’s pugilistic populism in a key swing state.
Jackson planned to join Trump at a rally Saturday in Perry, in what would be his second appearance with the president in the closing stretch of the campaign.

“My father left me at nine months old. My mother was a sixth-grade educated waitress with a severe alcohol problem,” Jackson said in the only debate of their general election campaign. “I had seven stepfathers before I was 12. I lived in the projects, went to 13 different schools, and lived in five different foster homes.”

He left college to start a business at 21. That led to Jackson Healthcare, a behemoth company that provides contract nurses and other workers to hospitals and health systems, including public entities that have helped fuel Jackson’s fortunes with taxpayer money.
At events with supporters, Jackson gets more personal.

“I have, because of my background, severe abandonment issues,” he told hundreds of voters in Cleveland, a conservative enclave in the north Georgia mountains. He turns that acknowledgment into a promise: “Let me tell you one thing: I will never abandon you.”

Rags-to-riches themes are not uncommon in politics, and it’s yielded Jackson’s campaign motto: “From foster care to billionaire.” But the scale is eye-popping, illuminated by the nearly $200 million Jackson has spent personally on the campaign. That puts him among the largest self-funding candidates in the history of American elections.
But on that score, too, Jackson tries to soften the caricature of the billionaire executive.
“It’s not my money,” he said in a northern suburb of Atlanta. Jackson calls his fortune “God’s money” and says that “my job is to have kingdom impact” with it.
“The reason I have spent so much money to do this,” he said, is to “help 11 million Georgians, to keep them from struggling.”

Jackson launched his bid as a relative unknown, though Capitol insiders knew him because of Jackson Healthcare, its lucrative state contracts and his lobbying interest in healthcare, business and tax policy.
The Republican primary field featured a trio of statewide elected officials, including Lt. Gov. Burt Jones, who won Trump’s endorsement in August 2025 , before Jackson got in.

body_zh: 共和党亿万富翁里克·杰克逊在寻求领导佐治亚州时正在走钢丝，与特朗普走钢丝 - ABC News
共和党亿万富翁里克·杰克逊在寻求领导佐治亚州时正在走钢丝。
里克·杰克逊希望成为佐治亚州州长，共和党亿万富翁承诺为工人阶级选民而战
亚特兰大——他并不是第一个向工人阶级选民承诺他将在公职上为他们而战的亿万富翁。佐治亚州州长共和党候选人里克·杰克逊甚至将自己比作入主椭圆形办公室的房地产大亨。
但杰克逊的道路与唐纳德·特朗普不同，这位 72 岁的医疗保健巨头和投资者在他的第一次竞选中带来了截然不同的形象。与出身富裕的特朗普不同，杰克逊早年在寄养家庭中度过，然后在年轻时创办了他的第一家公司。
现在，他想利用自己与总统的相似之处和对比，他正在用自己的大量竞选资金和个人故事来应对这一挑战，以增强他对选民的吸引力。
“我一直生活在贫困之中，”杰克逊说。 “当你没有吃饭的时候，你永远不会忘记这一点，你也不会忘记那些正在挣扎的人们。”
民主党候选人、亚特兰大前市长凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯 (Keisha Lance Bottoms) 对杰克逊的利他主义主张提出质疑，她将 11 月 3 日的选举视为一种考验，看看另一种更温和的保守亿万富翁政治是否能够补充甚至对抗特朗普在关键摇摆州的好斗民粹主义。
杰克逊计划周六与特朗普一起参加在佩里举行的集会，这将是他在竞选最后阶段第二次与总统一起露面。
“我的父亲在我九个月大时就离开了我。我的母亲是一名受过六年级教育的女服务员，有严重的酗酒问题，”杰克逊在大选活动的唯一一场辩论中说道。 “我 12 岁之前就有了 7 个继父。我住在这些项目中，上过 13 所不同的学校，住在 5 个不同的寄养家庭。”
21 岁时，他离开大学开始创业。这导致了杰克逊医疗保健公司 (Jackson Healthcare) 的诞生，这是一家向医院和卫生系统提供合同护士和其他工作人员的庞然大物，其中包括用纳税人的钱帮助杰克逊发家致富的公共实体。
在与支持者的活动中，杰克逊变得更加个性化。
“由于我的背景，我有严重的遗弃问题，”他对克利夫兰的数百名选民说，克利夫兰是佐治亚州北部山区的保守派飞地。他将这种承认变成了承诺：“让我告诉你一件事：我永远不会抛弃你。”
白手起家的主题在政治中并不罕见，这也催生了杰克逊的竞选座右铭：“从寄养家庭到亿万富翁。”但从杰克逊个人在竞选活动上花费的近 2 亿美元来看，其规模令人瞠目结舌。这使他成为美国选举历史上自筹资金最多的候选人之一。
但在这一点上，杰克逊也试图软化这位亿万富翁高管的漫画形象。
“这不是我的钱，”他在亚特兰大北郊说道。杰克逊称他的财富为“上帝的钱”，并表示“我的工作就是用它来影响王国”。
“我花这么多钱来做这件事的原因，”他说，是为了“帮助 1100 万格鲁吉亚人，让他们不再陷入困境。”
杰克逊在发起竞选时相对默默无闻，尽管国会内部人士因为杰克逊医疗保健公司、其利润丰厚的州合同以及他对医疗保健、商业和税收政策的游说兴趣而认识他。
共和党初选由三名全州民选官员组成，其中包括副州长伯特·琼斯(Burt Jones)，他在杰克逊上任之前于 2025 年 8 月赢得了特朗普的支持。
